title: Fix model attribution drift caused by transient alias remapping during regional failover
creator: Priya Patel
description: Symptoms: Intermittent spikes and sudden drops in per-model token charts observed during regional failovers and scheduled maintenance windows. Root report came from customer account dashboard where Model_X showed 3x tokens for a 12-minute window on 2026-01-20 and Model_Y showed corresponding undercount. Investigation uncovered event-attribution mismatches when routing-layer alias remapping propagates more quickly than the event-collector's model-alias cache TTL, causing short-lived events to be attributed to the wrong model ID in aggregate rollups and time-bucketed charts. Separately, delayed/backfilled ingestion overlapping with the transient alias state caused permanent misattribution in the hourly rollups because the backfill pipeline used the stale mapping snapshot at ingestion time.
root_cause_summary: Two independent timing issues combined: 1) routing service performs alias remap broadcast during failover which updates model_alias table across regions in <5s, but the event-collector caches alias->model_id mapping with a 60s TTL and writes the mapping used at event time into the event envelope. 2) Backfill worker replays late events and looks up alias-to-model mapping against the current mapping snapshot (not the mapping at original event timestamp), so if a backfill hits during a transient remapping window it writes the wrong model_id into the hourly rollup compute job. The aggregate pipeline then applies a compress/merge that double-counted some tokens when late events and live events overlapped.
proposed_fix_summary: Short-term: reduce event-collector alias cache TTL to 5s and make collectors embed both alias and canonical model_id at write-time. Mid-term: modify backfill pipeline to resolve alias at the event's original timestamp using an immutable alias-change log (append-only) so replays get historically-correct attribution. Long-term: add deterministic event provenance header and unify attribution logic in the aggregation service so it prefers canonical model_id when present and falls back to alias resolution only if necessary.
migration_plan: 1) Deploy alias-cache TTL change to collectors behind feature flag and monitor error/latency for 48h (canary region EU-west1 then roll to others)
2) Instrument collectors to include canonical_model_id field in event envelope; collector change behind feature flag and backwards-compatible with aggregate pipeline
3) Implement alias-change log: write small migration to export current alias change history and start appending every alias mutation going forward
4) Update backfill worker to consult alias-change log using event.timestamp and resolve canonical_model_id deterministically
5) Run controlled retroactive attribution pass for affected windows: run backfill for Jan 20 2026 00:00-06:00 UTC with idempotent safe-merge, write corrected hourly rollups to staging and validate
6) Promote corrected rollups to production during a low-traffic maintenance window with monitoring gates
7) Post-mortem dashboard and customer notifications for impacted customers
acceptance_criteria: Per-model hourly rollups show no >1% attribution variance vs immutable ground-truth benchmark for a 7-day rolling window after fix
Backfill runs for a 6-hour affected window produce identical canonical_model_id attribution when run twice (idempotency check)
No increase in median ingest latency >5% from collector changes in the first 72h of canary
Dashboards no longer show transient mirrored spikes between aliases during simulated failovers in staging
monitoring_queries: query:count_tokens_by_model_hourly WHERE model_id != canonical_model_id OVER last_7d
